newsitem.title: USA: Compaq to buy Tandem in $3 billion stock swap.
newsitem.headline: Compaq to buy Tandem in $3 billion stock swap.

text.p: Compaq Computer Corp., the world's leading supplier of personal computers, said Monday it agreed to acquire Tandem Computers Inc. for about $3 billion in stock, doubling its potential market.

Tandem's stock shot up more than 40 percent on the news while Compaq shares slid, both in heavy trading on the New York Stock Exchange. Tandem added $6.25 to $21.25 while Compaq lost $1.75 to $105.125.
Under terms of the definitive agreement, Tandem will become a wholly owned subsidiary of Compaq, which had been reported in merger talks with several companies.
Tandem, a $1.9 billion company based in Cupertino, Calif., manufactures fault-tolerant computer systems for processing on-line transactions. Founded in 1974, it employs nearly 7,000 people worldwide.

"Our total addressable market has been doubled to approximately $650 billion. This offers opportunity for significant revenue growth," Compaq Chief Executive Eckhard Pfeiffer said of the proposed merger.
Compaq, based in Houston, had worldwide sales of $18.1 billion last year.
Under the agreement, Compaq will issue some 29 million shares in exchange for all the stock of Tandem. The exchange ratio will be about 0.21 Compaq share for each share of Tandem.
Based on Compaq's trading price of $105.125, the total deal is worth about $3.05 billion, with each Tandem share valued at about $22.08.
Because the transaction will be a pooling of interests, Compaq's board of directors rescinded its previously announced share repurchase programme, the company said.
The deal is expected to be completed in the third quarter, subject to approval by Tandem shareholders, clearance under anti-trust law and other customary closing conditions.
Merger and acquisition specialists said the transaction probably would encounter little opposition.

"It is a straightforward deal between two companies that know each other very well. It is relatively issueless, though there is some question about whether or not it will hamper Compaq's growth rate," said one expert who requested anonymity.
Tandem Chairman Tom Perkins has been invited to join the Compaq board.
